items.title: The momentum of a potential presentation: the fibre derivative of the mechanical Lagrangian, the Cartesian momentum Mv and generalized momenta
items.statement:
Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]], in the
fixed inertial frame with adapted coordinates $(t,x)$ used there: $N\ge1$
labels with masses $m_{1},\dots,m_{N}>0$, open configuration domain
$Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$, time window $I_{0}$, mass operator $\mathsf M$
([[def-cm01-configuration]]), $C^{2}$ potential $U:I_{0}\times Q\to\mathbb R$
of dimension $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$ and residual forces $d$ of the standing
regularity ([[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]],
[[post-cm02-force-superposition]]). Dimensions are read by [[def-cm01-units]],
the Euclidean inner product of $\mathbb R^{3N}$ is [[def-euclidean-inner-product]],
and gradients and Jacobians are those of [[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]]
and [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]].

**(a) Cartesian momentum.** For a state $(t,x,v)\in I_{0}\times Q\times\mathbb R^{3N}$
define the **momentum of the labels** by

$$p(t,x,v):=\mathsf M v\;=\;(m_{1}v_{1},\dots,m_{N}v_{N}),$$

whose label components are $p_{i}=m_{i}v_{i}$ ([[def-cm01-configuration]]
clause (d)); its dimension is $\mu\ell\tau^{-1}$ (read in
$\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$). The space $\mathbb R^{3N}$ is
identified with its dual by the Euclidean inner product, so that $p$ is a
**covector** acting on a velocity $w$ by the dot product $p\cdot w$. The pair
$(x,p)$ is the **cotangent datum** of the state, and $I_{0}\times Q\times\mathbb R^{3N}$
with coordinates $(t,x,p)$ is the **momentum phase chart** of the
presentation.

**(b) Fibre derivative.** The **fibre derivative** (the velocity Legendre
coordinate) of the presentation is $p:=\mathcal L_{v}(t,x,v)$, the Legendre
map of the fibre-full chart $(O,L)$ of clause (c) of
[[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]], in the sense of
[[def-cm-legendre-map-in-a-time-dependent-chart]] (the chart data are those of
[[def-cm-time-dependent-lagrangian-and-action]]). Because $L=K-U$ with
$K'(v)=\mathsf Mv$ and $U$ independent of the velocity slot (clause (a) of
[[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]]), one has
$\mathcal L_{v}(t,x,v)=\mathsf Mv$: the fibre derivative and the momentum of
clause (a) are the same covector, and the Legendre map of the presentation is
$(t,x,v)\mapsto(t,x,\mathsf Mv)$.

**(c) Generalized momenta.** Let $X:\Omega\to Q$ be a generalized-coordinate
map of the model, with substituted Lagrangian $\widetilde L$, substituted
potential $\widetilde U$ and kinetic metric $G(q)=DX(q)^{\mathsf T}\mathsf M\,DX(q)$
([[def-cm07-generalized-coordinates-and-forces]] clauses (a)-(b),
[[def-matrix-product-and-identity-matrix]], [[def-transpose-of-a-matrix]]).
The **generalized momentum** of the presentation in the coordinates $X$ is
the covector

$$p(t,q,v):=\widetilde L_{v}(t,q,v)=G(q)v,$$

whose components $p_{a}=\partial\widetilde L/\partial v_{a}$ have dimension
$\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-1}\gamma_{a}^{-1}$ (action divided by the dimension
$\gamma_{a}$ of the coordinate $q_{a}$), while the **pairing**
$p\cdot v=\sum_{a}p_{a}v^{a}$ has dimension $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$. For the
Cartesian chart, $X=\mathrm{id}$, $\Omega=Q$, $G=\mathsf M$, and clause (c)
reduces to clause (a).

**(d) Status and warnings.** The item defines the momentum datum of a declared
presentation as a model object. It introduces no force law, no equation of
motion and no measured value; it depends on the declared chart and on the
declared coordinate dimensions $\gamma_{a}$, and it is independent of the
residual forces $d$ and of the normalization $U\mapsto U+c(t)$ of the
potential representative ([[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]]
clause (c)). The momentum is not in general mass times coordinate velocity: in
the coordinates $X$ it is $G(q)v$, and the identity $p_{i}=m_{i}v_{i}$ is
specific to Cartesian data. The evaluation of the velocity Hessian, the
invertibility of the fiberwise momentum map, the Hamiltonian of an inverse
branch and the evolution equations are the subject of the other items of this
page, not of this definition. All differentiability classes are those of
[[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]].
items.physical_scope: The momentum datum of the framework's force branch with a declared potential presentation: the Cartesian momentum Mv of the labelled particles in an inertial frame, its identification with the fibre derivative of the mechanical Lagrangian, the generalized momenta G(q)v of a declared generalized-coordinate map, their dimensions and their pairings with velocities. The item defines model-derived objects only: it asserts no equation of motion, no conservation law, no inverse-Legendre branch and no measured value, and it does not claim that any apparatus is described by the potential branch.

references.title: D. Tong, Classical Dynamics (Cambridge lecture notes, January 2015 printing), Section 4.1, printed pages 80-84 (PDF pages 86-90): the generalized momenta p_i = dL/dqdot_i, the warning that they coincide with the usual momentum only in Cartesian coordinates, and the phase space of coordinates and momenta

K. K. Likharev, Essential Graduate Physics, Part CM: Classical Mechanics (title page last edited September 1, 2026), Section 10.1, chapter pages 1-2: the generalized momentum p_j = dL/dqdot_j and the Hamiltonian defined from it

I. Stewart, Advanced Classical Mechanics (MIT 8.09/8.309 Fall 2014 course text), Section 1.2, printed pages 8-9 (PDF pages 11-12): canonical momenta promoted to coordinates, p_i = dL/dqdot_i, and the phase space of coordinates and momenta

G. J. Sussman and J. Wisdom, Structure and Interpretation of Classical Mechanics, second edition (MIT Press, 2014/2015), Section 3.1.1: the momentum state function as the partial derivative of the Lagrangian and the Legendre transformation replacing velocity dependence by momentum dependence

items.title: Velocity-regular potential presentations: the velocity Hessian of the mechanical Lagrangian, regular states and regular charts
items.statement:
Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]] in the
fixed inertial frame with adapted coordinates $(t,x)$: masses
$m_{1},\dots,m_{N}>0$, open configuration domain $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$,
time window $I_{0}$, mass operator $\mathsf M$
([[def-cm01-configuration]]), $C^{2}$ potential $U$ and residual forces $d$ of
the standing regularity ([[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]],
[[post-cm02-force-superposition]]). Dimensions are read by
[[def-cm01-units]], and the Euclidean gradients and second partial derivatives
in the velocity slot are those of [[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]] and
[[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]].

**(a) Velocity Hessian.** Let $(O,L)$ be the fibre-full time-dependent
Lagrangian chart of clause (c) of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]]
and let $\widetilde L$ be the substituted Lagrangian of a generalized-coordinate
map $X:\Omega\to Q$ ([[def-cm07-generalized-coordinates-and-forces]]). The
**velocity Hessian** of the presentation in Cartesian data is the matrix
$L_{vv}(t,x,v)\in M_{3N}(\mathbb R)$ of second partial derivatives of $L$ in
its third slot at $(t,x,v)$; in the coordinates $X$ it is the matrix
$\widetilde L_{vv}(t,q,v)$ of second partial derivatives of $\widetilde L$ in
its third slot. Invertibility of the Hessian is invertibility of a linear map
in the sense of [[def-invertible-matrix-and-general-linear-group]], read by
[[cor-square-matrix-invertible-iff-determinant-is-a-unit]] through the
determinant, and matrices act on vectors by
[[def-matrix-product-and-identity-matrix]] and [[def-linear-map]];
transposes are those of [[def-transpose-of-a-matrix]].

**(b) Regular states and regular presentations.** The presentation is
**velocity-regular at the state** $(t,x,v)$ of the Cartesian chart when
$\det L_{vv}(t,x,v)\neq0$, and **velocity-regular at the state** $(t,q,v)$ of
the chart of $X$ when $\det\widetilde L_{vv}(t,q,v)\neq0$. It is **regular on
a chart** when it is velocity-regular at every state of that chart, and
**regular** when this holds on the chart under discussion. This is exactly the
regularity of [[def-cm-legendre-map-in-a-time-dependent-chart]] instantiated
at the corresponding fibre-full chart: the Legendre map is regular at a state
precisely when its velocity Hessian there is nonsingular. The evaluation of
the Hessian for the model's mechanical presentations, and the conclusion that
those presentations are regular at every state, are proved on this page (the
local Legendre theorem) and are not part of this definition.

**(c) Local inverse branch data.** Let the presentation be velocity-regular
at a state $z$ of a chart with Legendre map $\mathbb F$ and momentum image
$z':=\mathbb F(z)$. A **local inverse branch at $z$** is a pair of open sets
$W\ni z$ and $W'\ni z'$ together with a $C^{1}$ map $v_{W}:W'\to W$ that is
inverse to $\mathbb F|_{W}:W\to W'$; equivalently, $\mathbb F|_{W}$ is a
$C^{1}$ diffeomorphism onto $W'$ in the sense of
[[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]. A local inverse branch assigns
to every momentum covector in $W'$ a state in $W$ whose fibre derivative is
that covector. Whether such a branch exists at a regular state, and when it
extends to a global fibre inverse, are conditional statements of the local
and global Legendre theorems of this page.

**(d) Status.** The item fixes the regularity vocabulary of the presentation
and the data used by the local Legendre theorem; it asserts no existence of
inverse branches, no hyperregularity, no equation of motion and no empirical
value. The regularity condition is a condition on the declared chart data
$(U,\mathsf M)$ and, in the coordinates $X$, on the declared map $X$; no
such condition is imposed on the residual forces $d$, which do not enter the
velocity Hessian of $L=K-U$.
items.physical_scope: The regularity vocabulary of a potential presentation of the framework's force branch: the velocity Hessian of the mechanical Lagrangian in Cartesian data and in a declared generalized-coordinate chart, velocity-regular states and regular presentations, and the local inverse branch data attached to a regular state. The item defines conditions on the model's chart data and fixes the notation used by the local Legendre theorem and by the Hamiltonian items; it asserts no existence of a global momentum inverse, no equation of motion and no measured value.

references.title: D. Tong, Classical Dynamics (Cambridge lecture notes, January 2015 printing), Section 4.1.1, printed pages 82-83 (PDF pages 88-89): the requirement that the velocity-momentum relation be inverted, and the convexity discussion accompanying the Legendre transform

D. Cline, Variational Principles in Classical Mechanics (2nd edition, University of Rochester River Campus Libraries, open textbook, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0), Sections 8.2-8.3: the conversion of Lagrange's equations into Hamiltonian form hinges on the inversion of the generalized-momentum relation

G. J. Sussman and J. Wisdom, Structure and Interpretation of Classical Mechanics, second edition (MIT Press, 2014/2015), Section 3.1.1: the Legendre transform cannot be implemented in general because it requires the functional inverse of the velocity derivative, which for velocity-quadratic Lagrangians is explicitly invertible

I. Stewart, Advanced Classical Mechanics (MIT 8.09/8.309 Fall 2014 course text), Section 1.2, printed page 9 (PDF page 12): for Lagrangians quadratic in the velocities the momenta are linear in the velocities and the inverse T-hat inverse exists because the kinetic matrix is positive definite

items.title: Hyperregular potential presentations and their inverse Legendre branches in the model's charts
items.statement:
Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]] with the
data and conventions of [[def-cm12-cotangent-momentum]]: masses
$m_{1},\dots,m_{N}>0$, open configuration domain $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$,
time window $I_{0}$, mass operator $\mathsf M$
([[def-cm01-configuration]]), $C^{2}$ potential $U$ and residual forces $d$ of
the standing regularity ([[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]],
[[post-cm02-force-superposition]]); dimensions are read by
[[def-cm01-units]] and differentiability classes are those of
[[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]].

**(a) Cartesian chart.** The presentation is **hyperregular on the Cartesian
chart** when for every $(t,x)\in I_{0}\times Q$ the fibre momentum map

$$\mathbb F_{t,x}:\mathbb R^{3N}\longrightarrow\mathbb R^{3N},\qquad \mathbb F_{t,x}(v):=L_{v}(t,x,v)=\mathsf Mv,$$

is a bijection of $\mathbb R^{3N}$ onto $\mathbb R^{3N}$ and the inverse
assignment

$$v:I_{0}\times Q\times\mathbb R^{3N}\longrightarrow\mathbb R^{3N},\qquad L_{v}\bigl(t,x,v(t,x,p)\bigr)=p,$$

is defined on the whole momentum phase chart $I_{0}\times Q\times\mathbb R^{3N}$
and is of class $C^{1}$. In that case $v$ is the **inverse Legendre branch**
of the presentation on the Cartesian chart. Hyperregularity of a chart is
exactly hyperregularity of its fibre-full Lagrangian in the sense of
[[def-cm-legendre-map-in-a-time-dependent-chart]], read through the
identification of the fibre derivative with the momentum of
[[def-cm12-cotangent-momentum]].

**(b) Generalized-coordinate chart.** Let $X:\Omega\to Q$ be a
generalized-coordinate map with substituted Lagrangian $\widetilde L$ and
kinetic metric $G$ ([[def-cm07-generalized-coordinates-and-forces]]). The
presentation is **hyperregular on the chart of $X$** when for every
$(t,q)\in I_{0}\times\Omega$ the fibre map
$v\mapsto\widetilde L_{v}(t,q,v)=G(q)v$ is a bijection of $\mathbb R^{r}$ onto
$\mathbb R^{r}$ and the inverse assignment
$v(t,q,p)$ on $I_{0}\times\Omega\times\mathbb R^{r}$ is of class $C^{1}$; $v$
is then the **inverse Legendre branch** in the coordinates $X$. Linear maps
and bijectivity are read by [[def-linear-map]], and the pairing of momentum
covectors with velocities is the Euclidean pairing of
[[def-euclidean-inner-product]].

**(c) Status.** The item defines the hyperregularity condition and the branch
objects for the two chart types of the model. It asserts no branch existence,
no relation between regularity [[def-cm12-regularity]] and hyperregularity, no
equation of motion and no empirical value. Whether the model's mechanical
presentations are hyperregular is a conditional statement of this page (the
global Legendre theorem for the mechanical branch), and a presentation that is
regular at every state but whose fibre momentum map is not surjective shows
that the condition is not automatic; the companion page's example
$\mathcal L(v)=e^{v}$ witnesses this separation.
items.physical_scope: Hyperregularity of a potential presentation of the force branch and the vocabulary of its inverse Legendre branch: invertibility of the fibrewise velocity-to-momentum map, the globally defined inverse branch and its momentum phase chart in Cartesian data and in a declared generalized-coordinate chart. The item defines a condition on the model's declared chart data and the branch objects used by the Hamiltonian definition; it asserts neither that the model's presentations satisfy the condition nor any equation of motion, conservation law or measured value.

references.title: D. Tong, Classical Dynamics (Cambridge lecture notes, January 2015 printing), Section 4.1.2, printed pages 83-84 (PDF pages 89-90): the elimination of the velocities in favour of the momenta by inverting p_i = dL/dqdot_i, and the Hamiltonian defined from the inverse relation

D. Cline, Variational Principles in Classical Mechanics (2nd edition, University of Rochester River Campus Libraries, open textbook, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0), Section 8.2: the Legendre transform states that the inverse formula can always be written as a first-order derivative, with the passive variables related by the corresponding partial derivatives

G. J. Sussman and J. Wisdom, Structure and Interpretation of Classical Mechanics, second edition (MIT Press, 2014/2015), Section 3.1.1: the Legendre transformation provides an inverse that gives the velocities in terms of the momenta, and the velocity-quadratic case is explicitly invertible

I. Stewart, Advanced Classical Mechanics (MIT 8.09/8.309 Fall 2014 course text), Section 1.2, printed page 9 (PDF page 12): inverting the relation p-vector = a-vector + T-hat dot qdot-vector gives qdot-vector = T-hat inverse dot (p-vector - a-vector)

items.title: The Hamiltonian of a hyperregular potential presentation: the Legendre transform of the mechanical Lagrangian, its domain and its dimensions
items.statement:
Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]] with the
data and conventions of [[def-cm12-cotangent-momentum]]: masses
$m_{1},\dots,m_{N}>0$, open configuration domain $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$,
time window $I_{0}$, mass operator $\mathsf M$
([[def-cm01-configuration]]), $C^{2}$ potential $U$ and residual forces $d$ of
the standing regularity ([[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]],
[[post-cm02-force-superposition]]); dimensions are read by
[[def-cm01-units]] and the Euclidean pairing is
[[def-euclidean-inner-product]].

**(a) Cartesian Hamiltonian.** Assume the presentation is hyperregular on the
Cartesian chart, with inverse Legendre branch
$v:I_{0}\times Q\times\mathbb R^{3N}\to\mathbb R^{3N}$
([[def-cm12-hyperregularity]], [[def-cm-legendre-map-in-a-time-dependent-chart]]).
The **Hamiltonian of the presentation on the Cartesian chart** is the function

$$H:I_{0}\times Q\times\mathbb R^{3N}\longrightarrow\mathbb R,\qquad H(t,x,p):=p\cdot v(t,x,p)-L\bigl(t,x,v(t,x,p)\bigr),$$

where $p\cdot v(t,x,p)$ is the Euclidean pairing of the momentum covector
with the inverse-branch velocity ([[def-cm12-cotangent-momentum]],
[[def-euclidean-inner-product]]). The momentum phase chart
$I_{0}\times Q\times\mathbb R^{3N}$ with coordinates $(t,x,p)$ is the
**Hamiltonian phase chart** of the presentation on the Cartesian chart.

**(b) Generalized-coordinate Hamiltonian.** Let $X:\Omega\to Q$ be a
generalized-coordinate map with substituted Lagrangian $\widetilde L$, kinetic
metric $G$ and inverse Legendre branch $v$ on
$I_{0}\times\Omega\times\mathbb R^{r}$ ([[def-cm07-generalized-coordinates-and-forces]],
[[def-cm12-hyperregularity]]). The **Hamiltonian of the presentation in the
coordinates $X$** is

$$\widetilde H:I_{0}\times\Omega\times\mathbb R^{r}\longrightarrow\mathbb R,\qquad \widetilde H(t,q,p):=p\cdot v(t,q,p)-\widetilde L\bigl(t,q,v(t,q,p)\bigr).$$

For the Cartesian chart, $X=\mathrm{id}$ and $\widetilde H=H$; the general
definition is the same formula applied to the substituted fibre-full chart.

**(c) Dimensions and conventions.** Each term of the defining difference has
dimension $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$ (energy): the pairing $p\cdot v$ multiplies
$\mu\ell\tau^{-1}$ by $\ell\tau^{-1}$ in Cartesian data
([[def-cm12-cotangent-momentum]]), and $L$ has energy dimension
([[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]]). In the coordinates $X$ the
pairing is dimensionally consistent for every declared coordinate dimension
$\gamma_{a}$ and the dimension is unchanged. The Hamiltonian is $C^{1}$ on
its domain, being a sum of products of $C^{1}$ maps
([[thm-ck-euclidean-maps-closed-under-algebra-and-composition]],
[[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]). The pairing is the coordinate
Euclidean product; no metric on momentum space and no symplectic form is
introduced by this definition.

**(d) Dependence and status.** The Hamiltonian depends on the declared chart,
on the declared inverse Legendre branch (when more than one branch exists it
is part of the data, as in [[def-cm12-hyperregularity]]) and on the potential
representative: replacing $U$ by $U+c(t)$ leaves the branch unchanged and
replaces $L$ by $L-c(t)$, hence replaces $H$ by $H+c(t)$
([[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]] clause (c),
[[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]] clause (b)). It asserts no
equation of motion, no conservation property and no measured value; the
explicit kinetic-plus-potential form of $H$ for the mechanical branch, the
equivalence of its equations with the model's equation of motion and its
relation to the mechanical energy are the theorems of this page. Matrix
identities used by those theorems are read through
[[def-matrix-product-and-identity-matrix]].
items.physical_scope: The Hamiltonian datum of a hyperregular potential presentation: the Legendre transform p.v - L evaluated on the declared inverse Legendre branch, in Cartesian data and in a declared generalized-coordinate chart, its momentum phase domain, its energy dimension and its dependence on the declared chart, branch and potential representative. The item defines a model-derived function only; it asserts no equation of motion, no conservation law and no measured value, and the explicit kinetic-plus-potential form for the mechanical branch is a theorem of this page, not part of the definition.

references.title: D. Tong, Classical Dynamics (Cambridge lecture notes, January 2015 printing), Section 4.1.2, printed pages 83-84 (PDF pages 89-90): the Hamiltonian H = sum_i p_i qdot_i - L with the velocities eliminated in favour of the momenta

K. K. Likharev, Essential Graduate Physics, Part CM: Classical Mechanics (title page last edited September 1, 2026), Section 10.1, chapter page 2 (PDF page 238): H = sum_j p_j qdot_j - L computed as a function of t, the coordinates and the generalized momenta

I. Stewart, Advanced Classical Mechanics (MIT 8.09/8.309 Fall 2014 course text), Section 1.2, printed pages 8-9 (PDF pages 11-12): the Legendre transformation H(q,p,t) = qdot_i p_i - L(q,qdot,t) and the general form for Lagrangians quadratic plus linear in the velocities

D. Cline, Variational Principles in Classical Mechanics (2nd edition, University of Rochester River Campus Libraries, open textbook, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0), Section 8.2: the function which is the Legendre transform of the Lagrangian is called the Hamiltonian function

items.title: The velocity Hessian of the mechanical Lagrangian and the local invertibility of its Legendre map in every chart of the model
items.statement:
Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]] with the
data and conventions of [[def-cm12-cotangent-momentum]]: masses
$m_{1},\dots,m_{N}>0$, open configuration domain $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$,
time window $I_{0}$, mass operator $\mathsf M$
([[def-cm01-configuration]]), $C^{2}$ potential
$U:I_{0}\times Q\to\mathbb R$ and residual forces $d$ of the standing
regularity ([[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]],
[[post-cm02-force-superposition]]). Let $X:\Omega\to Q$ be a
generalized-coordinate map with substituted Lagrangian $\widetilde L$ and
kinetic metric $G(q)=DX(q)^{\mathsf T}\mathsf M\,DX(q)$
([[def-cm07-generalized-coordinates-and-forces]]). Then:

1. **(velocity Hessian)** For every $(t,x,v)\in I_{0}\times Q\times\mathbb R^{3N}$
   one has $L_{v}(t,x,v)=\mathsf Mv$ and $L_{vv}(t,x,v)=\mathsf M$, and for
   every $(t,q,v)\in I_{0}\times\Omega\times\mathbb R^{r}$ one has
   $\widetilde L_{v}(t,q,v)=G(q)v$ and $\widetilde L_{vv}(t,q,v)=G(q)$. Both
   matrices are symmetric and positive definite; consequently the Cartesian
   presentation and the presentation in the coordinates $X$ are
   velocity-regular at every state in the sense of [[def-cm12-regularity]].

2. **(local inverse branch)** At every state $z$ of either chart there is a
   local inverse branch: open sets $W\ni z$ and
   $W'\ni\mathbb F(z)$ with $\mathbb F|_{W}:W\to W'$ a $C^{1}$
   diffeomorphism, where $\mathbb F$ is the Legendre map of the corresponding
   fibre-full chart ([[def-cm12-regularity]] clause (c),
   [[def-cm-legendre-map-in-a-time-dependent-chart]]).

The statement is conditional on the adopted force branch and on the declared
presentation; it asserts no global inverse Legendre branch on a momentum
fibre and no empirical content.
items.physical_scope: The Legendre map of a declared potential presentation of the force branch: the velocity Hessian of the mechanical Lagrangian in an inertial Cartesian chart and in a declared generalized-coordinate chart, its positivity, the resulting velocity-regularity at every state, and the existence of a local C^1 inverse branch at every state of those charts. The statement is a conditional deduction from the adopted force branch, the declared presentation and the cited mathematics; it asserts no global inverse branch on a momentum fibre, no equation of motion, no conservation law and no measured value.

references.title: D. Tong, Classical Dynamics (Cambridge lecture notes, January 2015 printing), Sections 4.1.1-4.1.3, printed pages 82-84 (PDF pages 88-90): inversion of p = dL/dqdot and the worked particle-in-a-potential case p = m r-dot, H = p^2/(2m) + V(r)

D. Cline, Variational Principles in Classical Mechanics (2nd edition, University of Rochester River Campus Libraries, open textbook, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0), Sections 8.2-8.3: the Legendre transform of the Lagrangian, the inversion of the generalized momentum, and the resulting Hamilton equations

G. J. Sussman and J. Wisdom, Structure and Interpretation of Classical Mechanics, second edition (MIT Press, 2014/2015), Sections 3.1 and 3.1.1: the Legendre transformation, its relation to the functional inverse of the velocity derivative, and Hamilton's equations

I. Stewart, Advanced Classical Mechanics (MIT 8.09/8.309 Fall 2014 course text), Section 1.2, printed pages 8-9 (PDF pages 11-12): the Legendre transformation from L to H and the explicit inverse for Lagrangians quadratic in the velocities

items.title: Every potential presentation is hyperregular in its charts, with inverse branch $v = \mathsf M^{-1}p$ (or $G(q)^{-1}p$) and the explicit kinetic-plus-potential Hamiltonian
items.statement:
Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]] with the
data and conventions of [[def-cm12-cotangent-momentum]]: masses
$m_{1},\dots,m_{N}>0$, open configuration domain $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$,
time window $I_{0}$, mass operator $\mathsf M$
([[def-cm01-configuration]]), $C^{2}$ potential
$U:I_{0}\times Q\to\mathbb R$ and residual forces $d$ of the standing
regularity ([[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]],
[[post-cm02-force-superposition]]). Let $X:\Omega\to Q$ be a
generalized-coordinate map with substituted Lagrangian $\widetilde L$,
kinetic metric $G(q)=DX(q)^{\mathsf T}\mathsf M\,DX(q)$ and substituted
potential $\widetilde U(t,q)=U(t,X(q))$
([[def-cm07-generalized-coordinates-and-forces]]), and let $H$ and
$\widetilde H$ be the Hamiltonians of [[def-cm12-hamiltonian]]. Then:

1. **(Cartesian chart)** The fibre momentum map
   $\mathbb F_{t,x}(v)=\mathsf Mv$ is a bijection of $\mathbb R^{3N}$ onto
   $\mathbb R^{3N}$ for every $(t,x)\in I_{0}\times Q$, and the inverse
   Legendre branch is the $C^{2}$ map
   $v(t,x,p)=\mathsf M^{-1}p$ on the whole phase chart
   $I_{0}\times Q\times\mathbb R^{3N}$. Hence the presentation is
   hyperregular on the Cartesian chart in the sense of
   [[def-cm12-hyperregularity]], and the Hamiltonian of the branch is

$$H(t,x,p)=\tfrac12\,p\cdot\mathsf M^{-1}p+U(t,x),$$

with the dot product of [[def-euclidean-inner-product]],

   a $C^{2}$ function of dimension $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$.

2. **(generalized-coordinate chart)** The fibre map
   $v\mapsto G(q)v$ is a bijection of $\mathbb R^{r}$ onto $\mathbb R^{r}$
   for every $(t,q)\in I_{0}\times\Omega$, and the inverse Legendre branch is
   the $C^{2}$ map $v(t,q,p)=G(q)^{-1}p$ on
   $I_{0}\times\Omega\times\mathbb R^{r}$. Hence the presentation is
   hyperregular on the chart of $X$, and the Hamiltonian in the coordinates
   $X$ is

$$\widetilde H(t,q,p)=\tfrac12\,p\cdot G(q)^{-1}p+\widetilde U(t,q),$$

   a $C^{2}$ function of dimension $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$.

The statement is conditional on the adopted force branch and the declared
presentation; it asserts no equation of motion, no conservation law and no
empirical content.
items.physical_scope: Globality of the Legendre transformation of a declared potential presentation of the force branch: the velocity-to-momentum maps of the Cartesian chart and of a declared generalized-coordinate chart are C^2 bijections of each velocity fibre onto the full momentum fibre, with the explicit C^2 inverse branches v = M^{-1}p and v = G(q)^{-1}p, and the Hamiltonians of those branches have the explicit kinetic-plus-potential forms. The statement is a conditional deduction from the adopted force branch, the declared presentation and the cited mathematics; it asserts no equation of motion, no conservation law and no measured value.

items.title: Hamilton's equations of the mechanical presentation are equivalent to the model's equation of motion, with residual forces as momentum sources and the coordinate form on every chart
items.statement:
Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]] with the
data and conventions of [[def-cm12-cotangent-momentum]]: masses
$m_{1},\dots,m_{N}>0$, open configuration domain $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$,
time window $I_{0}$, mass operator $\mathsf M$
([[def-cm01-configuration]]), $C^{2}$ potential
$U:I_{0}\times Q\to\mathbb R$ and residual forces $d$ of the standing
regularity ([[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]],
[[post-cm02-force-superposition]]). Let $H$ be the Cartesian Hamiltonian of
[[def-cm12-hamiltonian]], let $X:\Omega\to Q$ be a generalized-coordinate map
with substituted Lagrangian $\widetilde L$, kinetic metric
$G(q)=DX(q)^{\mathsf T}\mathsf M\,DX(q)$, substituted potential
$\widetilde U(t,q)=U(t,X(q))$ and residual generalized force
$Q^{\mathrm{res}}(t,q,v)=DX(q)^{\mathsf T}d(t,X(q),DX(q)v)$, and let
$\widetilde H$ be the Hamiltonian in the coordinates $X$
([[def-cm07-generalized-coordinates-and-forces]],
[[def-cm12-hamiltonian]]). Let $J\subseteq I_{0}$ be a nonempty open interval
and let $x:J\to Q$ be a $C^{2}$ curve, with $p(t):=\mathsf Mx'(t)$
([[def-cm12-cotangent-momentum]]). Then:

1. **(potential branch)** Assume $d\equiv0$ on the state domain. The following
   are equivalent:
   (a) $x$ is a motion of the model on $J$
   ([[def-cm02-newtonian-flow]]);
   (b) $(x,p)$ satisfies $x'(t)=H_{p}\bigl(t,x(t),p(t)\bigr)$ and
   $p'(t)=-H_{x}\bigl(t,x(t),p(t)\bigr)$ for every $t\in J$;
   (c) for all reals $a<b$ with $[a,b]\subseteq J$ the restriction
   $x|_{[a,b]}$ is stationary for the action $S$ of $L$ on $[a,b]$
   ([[def-cm-time-dependent-lagrangian-and-action]],
   [[pthm-cm07-euler-lagrange-equations]]).

2. **(residual forces)** For a $C^{2}$ curve $x:J\to Q$ with
   $p(t)=\mathsf Mx'(t)$ the following are equivalent:
   (a) $\mathsf Mx''(t)=-\nabla_{x}U\bigl(t,x(t)\bigr)+d\bigl(t,x(t),x'(t)\bigr)$
   for every $t\in J$;
   (b) $x'(t)=H_{p}\bigl(t,x(t),p(t)\bigr)$ and
   $p'(t)=-H_{x}\bigl(t,x(t),p(t)\bigr)+d\bigl(t,x(t),\mathsf M^{-1}p(t)\bigr)$
   for every $t\in J$.

3. **(coordinate form)** Let $q:J\to\Omega$ be a $C^{2}$ curve and put
   $p(t):=G(q(t))q'(t)$. Then the declared Lagrange equations of
   [[def-cm07-generalized-coordinates-and-forces]] clause (e) are equivalent
   to the Hamilton system of $\widetilde H$: for every $t\in J$,

$$\Lambda(\widetilde L)(q)(t)=Q^{\mathrm{res}}\bigl(t,q(t),q'(t)\bigr)\ \Longleftrightarrow\ q'(t)=\widetilde H_{p}\bigl(t,q(t),p(t)\bigr),\quad p'(t)=-\widetilde H_{q}\bigl(t,q(t),p(t)\bigr)+Q^{\mathrm{res}}\bigl(t,q(t),q'(t)\bigr);$$

   in particular, when $d\equiv0$ the vanishing of the Lagrange operator is
   equivalent to $q'=\widetilde H_{p}$ and $p'=-\widetilde H_{q}$.

4. **(constraint elimination)** Assume in addition that $d\equiv0$ and that
   $X$ is a parametrization of a scleronomic regular holonomic-constraint
   locus in the sense of [[def-cm07-generalized-coordinates-and-forces]]
   clause (d), with the ideal-reaction law of
   [[post-cm06-ideal-reaction-law]]. Then the equivalent conditions of
   clause 3 with $Q^{\mathrm{res}}\equiv0$ hold for $q$ if and only if
   $x=X\circ q$ is a constrained motion of the model with an ideal reaction
   ([[pthm-cm07-lagrangian-reduction-of-ideal-constraints]]).

The statement is conditional on the adopted force branch, the declared
presentation, the declared chart and, in clause 4, the constraint datum and
ideal-reaction law; it asserts no existence or uniqueness of solutions, no
conservation law and no empirical content.
items.physical_scope: The equivalence between the Hamiltonian evolution of a declared potential presentation of the force branch and the model's equations of motion: on the potential branch the motions, the solutions of Hamilton's equations for the explicit branch Hamiltonian and the stationary curves of the action coincide; with residual forces the model's equation is equivalent to Hamilton's equations with the residual force as a momentum source; in a declared generalized-coordinate chart the declared Lagrange equations are equivalent to the Hamilton system, and for a scleronomic regular holonomic-constraint parametrization to the ideal constrained motion. The statement is a conditional deduction from the adopted force branch, the presentation and the cited mathematics; it makes no existence, uniqueness or empirical claim.

items.title: The mechanical Hamiltonian is the model's energy in the inertial chart, its balance is the energy balance, and the substituted-chart Hamiltonian is the energy of time-independent coordinates
items.statement:
Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]] with the
data and conventions of [[def-cm12-cotangent-momentum]]: masses
$m_{1},\dots,m_{N}>0$, open configuration domain $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$,
time window $I_{0}$, mass operator $\mathsf M$
([[def-cm01-configuration]]), $C^{2}$ potential
$U:I_{0}\times Q\to\mathbb R$ and residual forces $d$ of the standing
regularity ([[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]],
[[post-cm02-force-superposition]]). Let $H$ be the Cartesian Hamiltonian and
let, for a generalized-coordinate map $X:\Omega\to Q$ with substituted
Lagrangian $\widetilde L$, kinetic metric
$G(q)=DX(q)^{\mathsf T}\mathsf M\,DX(q)$ and substituted potential
$\widetilde U(t,q)=U(t,X(q))$, the symbol $\widetilde H$ denote the
Hamiltonian in the coordinates $X$ ([[def-cm12-hamiltonian]],
[[def-cm07-generalized-coordinates-and-forces]]). Let $J\subseteq I_{0}$ be a
nonempty open interval and let $x:J\to Q$ be a $C^{2}$ curve with
$p(t):=\mathsf Mx'(t)$; write $K(t)=\tfrac12\,x'(t)\cdot\mathsf Mx'(t)$ for
the kinetic energy and $E(t):=K(t)+U\bigl(t,x(t)\bigr)$ for the mechanical
energy along $x$ ([[def-cm03-centre-of-mass-and-momenta]],
[[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]]). Then:

1. **(the Hamiltonian is the energy)** For every $(t,x,p)\in I_{0}\times Q\times\mathbb R^{3N}$,
   $H(t,x,p)=\tfrac12\,p\cdot\mathsf M^{-1}p+U(t,x)$; consequently along every
   $C^{2}$ curve $x:J\to Q$ one has
   $H\bigl(t,x(t),p(t)\bigr)=\tfrac12\,x'(t)\cdot\mathsf Mx'(t)+U\bigl(t,x(t)\bigr)=E(t)$
   for every $t\in J$: on the Cartesian chart the Hamiltonian of the
   presentation is the model's mechanical energy.

2. **(balance and conservation)** If $x$ is a motion of the model
   ([[def-cm02-newtonian-flow]]) with evaluated residual forces
   $\mathfrak d_{i}(t):=d_{i}\bigl(t,x(t),x'(t)\bigr)$, then
   $t\mapsto H\bigl(t,x(t),p(t)\bigr)$ is differentiable on $J$ and

$$\frac{d}{dt}H\bigl(t,x(t),p(t)\bigr)=\partial_{t}U\bigl(t,x(t)\bigr)+\sum_{i=1}^{N}\bigl\langle\mathfrak d_{i}(t),\,x_{i}'(t)\bigr\rangle\qquad(t\in J);$$

   in particular, if $\partial_{t}U\equiv0$ on $I_{0}\times Q$ and
   $d\equiv0$, then $H\bigl(t,x(t),p(t)\bigr)$ is constant on $J$.

3. **(time-independent coordinates)** Let $X:\Omega\to Q$ be a
   generalized-coordinate map and let $q:J\to\Omega$ be a $C^{2}$ curve with
   $x:=X\circ q$ and $p(t):=G(q(t))q'(t)$. Then
   $\widetilde H(t,q,p)=\tfrac12\,p\cdot G(q)^{-1}p+\widetilde U(t,q)$ and

$$\widetilde H\bigl(t,q(t),p(t)\bigr)=\tfrac12\,q'(t)\cdot G\bigl(q(t)\bigr)q'(t)+\widetilde U\bigl(t,q(t)\bigr)=K(t)+U\bigl(t,x(t)\bigr)=E(t):$$

   the substituted-chart Hamiltonian of the induced configuration curve is
   the same mechanical energy of the model.

The statement is conditional on the adopted force branch and the declared
presentation; it asserts no measured value, no conservation outside the
stated hypotheses and no identity between $H$ and the mechanical energy for
charts other than those of clauses 1 and 3.
items.physical_scope: The relation between the Hamiltonian of a declared potential presentation of the force branch and the model's mechanical energy: in the inertial Cartesian chart the branch Hamiltonian equals K + U along every curve, its time derivative along a motion is the explicit time dependence of the potential plus the power of the residual forces, and it is constant for a static potential with no residual forces; in a time-independent generalized-coordinate chart the substituted Hamiltonian is the same mechanical energy of the induced configuration curve. The statement is a conditional deduction from the adopted force branch, the presentation and the cited mathematics; it asserts no measured value and no conservation outside the stated hypotheses.

title: Legendre transformation and Hamiltonian mechanics — Examples

items.title: Positive kinetic metric: the fibre map $p = \mathsf Mv$, the Hamiltonian and Hamilton's equations on explicit one- and two-label data
items.statement:
**(a) One label in a uniform field.** Declare the one-label model of the force
branch of [[post-cm02-force-superposition]] with $N=1$, mass $m>0$, time
window $I_{0}=\mathbb R$, configuration domain $Q=\mathbb R^{3}$ and potential
$U(t,x):=mgx_{3}$ with constant acceleration magnitude $g>0$, $[g]=\ell\tau^{-2}$, read in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$, with no residual forces; the force map
is $F=(0,0,-mg)$ and the mechanical Lagrangian is
$L(t,x,v)=\tfrac12m\lvert v\rvert_{2}^{2}-mgx_{3}$
([[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]],
[[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]]). Then:

1. the momentum of the presentation is $p=\mathsf Mv=mv$
   ([[def-cm12-cotangent-momentum]]), the presentation is hyperregular on the
   Cartesian chart with inverse branch $v=p/m$
   ([[pthm-cm12-mechanical-hyperregularity]]), and the Hamiltonian is
   $$H(t,x,p)=\frac{\lvert p\rvert_{2}^{2}}{2m}+mgx_{3}.$$
2. Hamilton's equations $\dot x=H_{p}$, $\dot p=-H_{x}$ read
   $\dot x=p/m$, $\dot p=(0,0,-mg)$, so that $m\ddot x=\dot p=(0,0,-mg)$:
   the system is equivalent to the model's equation of motion and the
   potential is the uniform field ([[pthm-cm12-hamilton-equivalence]]).
3. for every datum $(0,x_{0},v_{0})$, where $x_0\in\mathbb R^3$ is the initial position (metres) and $v_0\in\mathbb R^3$ the initial coordinate velocity (metres per second), the curve
   $$x(t):=x_{0}+v_{0}t-\tfrac12gt^{2}e_{3},\qquad e_{3}=(0,0,1),$$
   is the maximal motion of the model through that datum, defined for all
   real times; its velocity is $v_{0}-gte_{3}$ and its momentum is
   $m\bigl(v_{0}-gte_{3}\bigr)$.

**(b) Two labels with unequal masses.** Declare instead the free two-label
model $N=2$, masses $m_{1},m_{2}>0$, $I_{0}=\mathbb R$, $Q=\mathbb R^{6}$ and
zero force map, so that $U\equiv0$. Then $\mathsf M(v_{1},v_{2})=(m_{1}v_{1},m_{2}v_{2})$,
the Hamiltonian is $H=\lvert p_{1}\rvert_{2}^{2}/(2m_{1})+\lvert p_{2}\rvert_{2}^{2}/(2m_{2})$,
the inverse branch is $v=\mathsf M^{-1}p=(p_{1}/m_{1},p_{2}/m_{2})$, and
Hamilton's equations are $\dot x_{i}=p_{i}/m_{i}$, $\dot p_{i}=0$: each label
moves uniformly in a straight line, and the fibre map is a linear isomorphism
whose inverse is not a scalar multiple of the identity when $m_{1}\neq m_{2}$.

All quantities are model values of the declared idealizations; no measurement
is reported.

All quantities are model values of the declared idealizations; no measurement is reported.

items.title: The planar pendulum in Hamiltonian form: kinetic metric $ml^{2}$, substituted Hamiltonian $p^{2}/(2ml^{2}) - mgl\cos\theta$ and the reduced equation
items.statement:
Declare one particle label of mass $m>0$ in the force branch of [[post-cm02-force-superposition]], with time window $\mathbb R$, ambient configuration domain $Q=\mathbb R^3$, potential $U(x,y,z)=mgy$, constant $g>0$, and no residual force. Thus the force is $(0,-mg,0)$. Fix $l>0$ and impose the scleronomic regular constraint
$$\mathcal G(x,y,z)=(x^2+y^2-l^2,z)=0,$$
with the ideal-reaction law of [[post-cm06-ideal-reaction-law]]. Its locus is the full circle $N=\{x^2+y^2=l^2,z=0\}$. Here $m$ is a mass in kilograms, $l$ a length in metres, and $g$ an acceleration magnitude in metres per second squared; their dimensions are $\mu$, $\ell$, and $\ell\tau^{-2}$. The two components of $\mathcal G$ have dimensions $\ell^2$ and $\ell$, respectively. Write $G_{\mathrm{kin}}$ for the kinetic metric, to distinguish it from $\mathcal G$.

The full angular variable is an equivalence class $[\theta]\in\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z)$, with $\theta\sim\theta+2\pi k$, $k\in\mathbb Z$. The smooth periodic map
$$X(\theta)=(l\sin\theta,-l\cos\theta,0)$$
descends to the circle of constrained configurations; this identification is the rescaled and rotated circle parametrization of [[thm-real-line-mod-integers-is-homeomorphic-to-the-unit-circle]]. It is not a one-to-one map from $\mathbb R$ and is not used as one global generalized-coordinate parametrization.

Instead use the two angular charts $\Omega_0=(-\pi,\pi)$ and $\Omega_\pi=(0,2\pi)$, with restrictions $X_0,X_\pi$ of $X$. The ambient open sets
$$Q_0=\mathbb R^3\setminus\{(0,y,z):y\ge0\},\qquad Q_\pi=\mathbb R^3\setminus\{(0,y,z):y\le0\}$$
satisfy $X_a(\Omega_a)=N\cap Q_a$ for $a=0,\pi$. Restrict the ambient force model and constraint datum to $Q_a$ when applying [[def-cm07-generalized-coordinates-and-forces]] clause (d). Each restricted map is a one-to-one $C^3$ parametrization with injective derivative, covering its constrained arc exactly once. The two arcs cover $N$. On each connected component of an overlap the angular coordinates differ by $2\pi k$, with derivative $1$; no chart uses the same constrained configuration twice.

In either angular chart, the following hold, with dimensionless radian angle $\theta$:

On each phase-coordinate chart $\Omega_a\times\mathbb R$ with coordinates $(\theta,p)$, define an alternating bilinear form on coordinate increments $u=(u_\theta,u_p)$ and $v=(v_\theta,v_p)$ in $\mathbb R^2$ by
$$\omega_a(u,v):=u_\theta v_p-v_\theta u_p.$$
The notation $d\theta\wedge dp$ below denotes this explicitly defined form field.

1. $G_{\mathrm{kin}}=ml^2$, $\widetilde U=-mgl\cos\theta$, and
   $$\widetilde L(\theta,\dot\theta)=\tfrac12ml^2\dot\theta^2+mgl\cos\theta.$$
2. The generalized momentum is $p=ml^2\dot\theta$, of dimension action $\mu\ell^2\tau^{-1}$. The fibre map is hyperregular with inverse $\dot\theta=p/(ml^2)$, and
   $$\widetilde H(\theta,p)=\frac{p^2}{2ml^2}-mgl\cos\theta$$
   is the mechanical energy of the constrained motion.
3. Hamilton's equations are $\dot\theta=p/(ml^2)$, $\dot p=-mgl\sin\theta$, equivalently $\theta''=-(g/l)\sin\theta$. Locally these are equivalent to the ideal constrained motion, with its reaction recovered by [[pthm-cm07-lagrangian-reduction-of-ideal-constraints]].
4. On overlaps $\theta_b=\theta_a+2\pi k$ and $p_b=p_a$. The Lagrangian, Hamiltonian, equations, and canonical form $d\theta\wedge dp$ therefore agree, so the local Hamilton systems give one global system on the phase cylinder
   $$\bigl(\mathbb R\times\mathbb R\bigr)/\bigl((\theta,p)\sim(\theta+2\pi k,p)\bigr).$$
   This retains the entire pendulum, including rotations crossing either chart cut. Equivalence with the ideal constrained equations is local at every time and hence holds along any constrained motion, without pretending that one real angular chart is globally injective.

All quantities are declared model data; no measurement is reported.
items.physical_scope: A worked check of the Hamiltonian reformulation on the planar pendulum of the framework: one label of mass m constrained without friction to a vertical circle of radius l under a uniform downward field, described by a two-chart angular atlas covering the entire circle, including rotations; the kinetic metric is ml^2, the substituted Hamiltonian is p^2/(2ml^2) - mgl cos(theta), Hamilton's equations reduce to theta-double-dot = -(g/l) sin(theta), and the system is equivalent to the ideal constrained motion with its reaction recovered by the elimination theorem. All quantities are model values of the declared idealization; no measurement is reported.

items.title: Shifted momentum from a total-derivative modification: $p' = p + F_x$, $H' = H - F_t$ and unchanged motion on explicit data
items.statement:
Declare the one-label model of the force branch of
[[post-cm02-force-superposition]] with $N=1$, mass $m>0$, time window
$I_{0}=\mathbb R$, configuration domain $Q=\mathbb R^{3}$, a $C^{2}$ potential
$U:\mathbb R\times Q\to\mathbb R$ and no residual forces; write
$L(t,x,v)=\tfrac12m\lvert v\rvert_{2}^{2}-U(t,x)$ for its mechanical
Lagrangian ([[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]],
[[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]]). Fix a real parameter $\alpha$
and the smooth function $F(t,x):=\alpha\,t\,x_{1}$ on the full time-configuration projection $\mathbb R\times Q$, and define

$$L'(t,x,v):=L(t,x,v)+F_{t}(t,x)+F_{x}(t,x)\cdot v=L(t,x,v)+\alpha x_{1}+\alpha t\,v_{1}.$$

The units are $[m]=\mu$, $[x]=\ell$, $[t]=\tau$, $[\alpha]=\mu\ell\tau^{-2}$ (force, newtons), and $[F]=\mu\ell^2\tau^{-1}$ (action). The free initial speed $q$ below has dimension $\ell\tau^{-1}$ and is read in metres per second. Then:

1. $L'$ is a fibre-full $C^{2}$ time-dependent Lagrangian chart with
   velocity gradient $L'_{v}(t,x,v)=mv+\alpha t\,e_{1}$, $e_{1}=(1,0,0)$; the
   fibre map $v\mapsto L'_{v}(t,x,v)$ is a $C^{2}$ bijection of $\mathbb R^{3}$
   onto itself with inverse $v=(p'-\alpha t\,e_{1})/m$, so $L'$ is
   hyperregular on its generic time-dependent chart ([[def-cm-legendre-map-in-a-time-dependent-chart]]) and its fibre
   derivative is the **shifted momentum**
   $$p'=p+\alpha t\,e_{1},\qquad p=mv,$$
   which differs from the mechanical momentum $mv$ whenever $\alpha t\neq0$.
2. the Hamiltonian of the branch of $L'$ is
   $$H'(t,x,p')=\frac{\lvert p'-\alpha t\,e_{1}\rvert_{2}^{2}}{2m}+U(t,x)-\alpha x_{1}=H\bigl(t,x,p'-\alpha t\,e_{1}\bigr)-\alpha x_{1},$$
   where $H$ is the Hamiltonian of the presentation
   ([[def-cm12-hamiltonian]], [[pthm-cm12-mechanical-hyperregularity]]);
3. the Hamilton systems of $H$ and $H'$ are equivalent under the shift
   $p'=p+\alpha t\,e_{1}$: $\dot x=H'_{p'}=(p'-\alpha t\,e_{1})/m$ and
   $\dot p'=-H'_{x}=-\nabla_{x}U+\alpha e_{1}$ hold exactly when
   $\dot x=p/m$ and $\dot p=-\nabla_{x}U$ hold, so both systems have the same
   $x$-curves, namely the motions of the model
   ([[pthm-cm12-hamilton-equivalence]],
   [[pthm-cm07-boundary-terms-and-gauge]]); the Euler-Lagrange expressions
   coincide, $E_{L'}(x)=E_{L}(x)$, and the actions differ by the endpoint
   value $\alpha\bigl(b\,x_{1}(b)-a\,x_{1}(a)\bigr)$;
4. on free data $U\equiv0$, with $m>0$, $\alpha\ne0$, initial position $x(0)=0$ and initial velocity $v(0)=(q,0,0)$ with $q>0$, the curves
   $$x(t)=(qt,0,0),\qquad p'(t)=(mq+\alpha t,0,0)$$
   solve the shifted Hamilton system, and along them
   $$H'(t,x(t),p'(t))=\tfrac12mq^2-\alpha qt,\qquad K(t)+U(t,x(t))=\tfrac12mq^2.$$
   Thus $H'$ differs from the mechanical energy for $t\ne0$ while the motion is unchanged. For the numerical instance $m=1\,\mathrm{kg}$ and $\alpha=1\,\mathrm N$ the same dimensionally explicit formulas apply.


All quantities are model values of the declared idealization; no measurement
is reported.
items.physical_scope: A worked check of the momentum shift produced by a total-derivative modification of a declared potential presentation: for a one-label model with mass m and a smooth gauge function F(t,x) = alpha t x_1 on the full chart projection, the modified chart Lagrangian has fibre derivative p' = p + alpha t e_1, shifted Hamiltonian H' = H - alpha x_1 read at the shifted momentum, and Hamilton system equivalent to the original one; an explicit free-particle computation shows H' differs from the mechanical energy while the motion is unchanged. All quantities are model values of the declared idealization; no measurement is reported.

items.title: Regular but not hyperregular: the Lagrangian $e^{v}$, its branch $H(p)=p\ln p-p$ on $p>0$ and the absent inverse at nonpositive momenta
items.statement:
Take $n=1$, $J=U=\mathbb R$, and consider the fibre-full $C^{2}$ chart
Lagrangian

$$\mathcal L:\mathbb R\times\mathbb R\times\mathbb R\longrightarrow\mathbb R,\qquad \mathcal L(t,q,v):=e^{v}$$

([[def-cm-legendre-map-in-a-time-dependent-chart]],
[[def-cm-time-dependent-lagrangian-and-action]]). Then:

1. $\mathcal L$ is regular on the chart: $\mathcal L_{v}(t,q,v)=e^{v}$ and
   $\mathcal L_{vv}(t,q,v)=e^{v}>0$ for every $(t,q,v)$, so the velocity
   Hessian is nonsingular at every state and the Legendre map is a local
   $C^{1}$ diffeomorphism at every state
   ([[lem-cm-legendre-map-local-invertibility]]).
2. $\mathcal L$ is **not** hyperregular on the chart: the fibre velocity map
   $v\mapsto e^{v}$ has image $(0,\infty)$ and is not a bijection of
   $\mathbb R$ onto $\mathbb R$, so there is no inverse branch defined on the
   whole momentum line; a momentum $p\le0$ is not the fibre derivative of any
   velocity, and no Hamiltonian of a branch is defined there
   ([[def-cm-legendre-map-in-a-time-dependent-chart]]).
3. on the momentum half-line $p>0$ the inverse branch is
   $v(p)=\ln p$, the **unique** real number with $e^{v(p)}=p$
   ([[cor-exponential-is-a-bijection-onto-positive-reals]]), and the
   Hamiltonian of that branch is

$$H:(0,\infty)\longrightarrow\mathbb R,\qquad H(p)=p\,v(p)-e^{v(p)}=p\ln p-p,$$

   with $H'(p)=\ln p=v(p)$ for every $p>0$; in particular the differential
   identity $H_{p}=v$ of [[prop-cm-hamiltonian-branch-identities]] clause 1
   holds on this branch even though the chart is not hyperregular.
4. for every nonempty open interval $I$ and every $C^{2}$ curve
   $q:I\to\mathbb R$ with $p(t):=e^{q'(t)}$ one has:
   $\dot q=H'(p)$ and $\dot p=0$ hold for all $t\in I$ if and only if the
   Euler-Lagrange expression of $\mathcal L$ vanishes,
   $E_{\mathcal L}(q)(t)=0$, for all $t\in I$.

The example is a pure chart computation: $\mathcal L=e^{v}$ is not of the
natural mechanical form $\tfrac12v^{\mathsf T}Gv+A\cdot v-V$, and no physical
interpretation of it is claimed.

references.title: D. Tong, Classical Dynamics (Cambridge lecture notes, January 2015 printing), Section 4.1.1, printed pages 82-83 (PDF pages 88-89): the inverse Legendre transform requires inverting the velocity-momentum relation, and the convexity picture for the existence of the inverse

G. J. Sussman and J. Wisdom, Structure and Interpretation of Classical Mechanics, second edition (MIT Press, 2014/2015), Section 3.1.1: the Legendre transform cannot be implemented in general because it requires the functional inverse of the velocity derivative

items.title: Moving coordinates: the substituted Hamiltonian of a spring on a uniformly moving support, its conservation and the non-conservation of the mechanical energy
items.statement:
Declare the one-label model of the force branch of
[[post-cm02-force-superposition]] with $N=1$, mass $m>0$, time window
$I_{0}=\mathbb R$, configuration domain $Q=\mathbb R^{3}$ and potential
$U(t,x):=\tfrac12k\bigl(x_{1}-v_{0}t-c\bigr)^{2}$ with constants $k>0$,
$v_{0}\in\mathbb R$ and $c\in\mathbb R$, and no residual forces: the label is
attached by a spring of stiffness $k$ to a support whose position is the
prescribed function $v_{0}t+c$, so the force map is
$F=\bigl(-k(x_{1}-v_{0}t-c),0,0\bigr)$ and the mechanical Lagrangian is
$L=K-U$ with $K(v)=\tfrac12m\lvert v\rvert_{2}^{2}$
([[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]],
[[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]]). Introduce the **co-moving
coordinates**
$X(t,y):=\bigl(y_{1}+v_{0}t+c,\ y_{2},\ y_{3}\bigr)$, a time-dependent
coordinate map with $X_{q}=I_{3}$, and the substituted Lagrangian
$L'(t,y,w):=L\bigl(t,X(t,y),\,X_{t}(t,y)+X_{q}(t,y)w\bigr)$. This $L'$ is a generic fibre-full time-dependent Lagrangian chart of [[def-cm-legendre-map-in-a-time-dependent-chart]]; it need not be a $K-U$ presentation in a static coordinate map. The model units are $[k]=\mu\tau^{-2}$ (newtons per metre), $[v_0]=\ell\tau^{-1}$ (metres per second), $[c]=[y_0]=\ell$ (metres), $[q]=\mu\ell\tau^{-1}$ (momentum, kilograms metres per second), and $[\omega]=\tau^{-1}$ (radians per second with dimensionless radians). Here $y_0$ and $q$ are initial co-moving position and first momentum, respectively. Then:
 
1. $L'(t,y,w)=\tfrac12m\bigl(w_{1}+v_{0}\bigr)^{2}+\tfrac12m\bigl(w_{2}^{2}+w_{3}^{2}\bigr)-\tfrac12ky_{1}^{2}$,
   its fibre derivative is
   $$p'=L'_{w}(t,y,w)=\bigl(m(w_{1}+v_{0}),\ mw_{2},\ mw_{3}\bigr),$$
   and the coordinate change reproduces the model's equation: a $C^{2}$ curve
   $y$ satisfies the Euler-Lagrange equation of $L'$ exactly when
   $x(t)=X(t,y(t))$ satisfies $m\ddot x_{1}=-k(x_{1}-v_{0}t-c)$, $m\ddot x_{2}=m\ddot x_{3}=0$
   ([[pthm-cm07-coordinate-covariance-of-the-equations]]).
2. $L'$ is hyperregular on its chart with inverse branch
   $w=\bigl(p'_{1}/m-v_{0},\ p'_{2}/m,\ p'_{3}/m\bigr)$ and Hamiltonian
   $$H'(t,y,p')=\frac{p'_{1}{}^{2}}{2m}-v_{0}p'_{1}+\frac{p'_{2}{}^{2}}{2m}+\frac{p'_{3}{}^{2}}{2m}+\frac{k}{2}y_{1}^{2} =\frac{\bigl(p'_{1}-mv_{0}\bigr)^{2}}{2m}+\frac{k}{2}y_{1}^{2}+\frac{p'_{2}{}^{2}+p'_{3}{}^{2}}{2m}-\frac{mv_{0}^{2}}{2},$$
   so that on the first coordinate the momentum $p'_{1}$ equals the inertial
   momentum $p_{1}=m\dot x_{1}$ of [[def-cm12-cotangent-momentum]] while the
   branch velocity is shifted,
   $\dot y_{1}=p'_{1}/m-v_{0}$.
3. Hamilton's equations of $H'$ are
   $\dot y_{1}=p'_{1}/m-v_{0}$, $\dot p'_{1}=-ky_{1}$, $\dot y_{i}=p'_{i}/m$,
   $\dot p'_{i}=0$ for $i=2,3$; they imply $m\ddot y_{1}=-ky_{1}$, equivalently
   $m\ddot x_{1}=-k(x_{1}-v_{0}t-c)$, so the co-moving description is
   equivalent to the model's motion and the induced curve $x$ is a motion
   ([[def-cm02-newtonian-flow]]).
4. along the solutions the Hamiltonian $H'$ is conserved — it has no explicit
   time dependence in the co-moving chart — while the model's mechanical
   energy $E=K+U$ obeys, on the first axis,
   $$H'=E-v_{0}p'_{1},\qquad E'(t)=-kv_{0}y_{1}(t).$$
   At any time when $v_{0}y_{1}(t)\neq0$, the energy derivative is nonzero;
   in particular, the displayed solution has nonconstant $E$ when
   $v_{0}y_{0}\neq0$. With data $y_{1}(0)=y_{0}$, $p'_{1}(0)=q$ and
   $\omega:=\sqrt{k/m}$ the explicit solution is
   $$y_{1}(t)=y_{0}\cos\omega t+\frac{q-mv_{0}}{m\omega}\sin\omega t,\qquad p'_{1}(t)=-m\omega y_{0}\sin\omega t+\bigl(q-mv_{0}\bigr)\cos\omega t+mv_{0}.$$
 
All quantities are model values of the declared idealization; the moving
support is a prescribed external mechanism, and no measurement is reported.
items.physical_scope: A worked check of the Hamiltonian description in a time-dependent chart: a one-label model with a spring whose equilibrium point is attached to a support moving uniformly at a prescribed velocity, described in the co-moving coordinate; the substituted Lagrangian has a velocity-linear term, the substituted Hamiltonian is conserved, it differs from the model's mechanical energy by the product of the support velocity and the momentum, and the mechanical energy changes at the rate of the explicit time dependence of the potential. All quantities are model values of the declared idealization; no measurement is reported.
